From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>

Date: 2026-11-08T09:07:00-08:00
Subject: Capacity buckets & deal rhythm — weekly orchestration

Team —

Following up from this morning's sales-finance-infra sync. The ask for this weekly thread is narrow: map the top 6 deals in the pipeline into capacity "buckets" (1-3 from Dedicated reservations, 4-6 elastic/burst), and flag timing risks by week-of-close so infra can queue provisioning.

I've attached a capacity_buckets_template.xlsx and a short playbook excerpt. Please populate by EOD so I can present the numbers in Friday's Exec FYI. Key fields we need per-deal: deal_id, expected close week, committed QPS (or expected token throughput), requested SLA band (p1/p2/p3), and whether they require private deployment.

Immediate asks:
- Ben: add the realistic burst eligibility and expected share of total tokens per deal.
- Laura: confirm finance's burn-rate threshold for moving a deal from bucket 3 -> 2.
- Michael: FYI to infra — note any provisioning lead times that might push a deal past the milestone.

I'll route the consolidated sheet to Acme (Sophie) once we have a consensus on buckets and timing.

Jordan
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_buckets_template.xlsx, capacity_playbook_v2.pdf

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.example.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-11-08T10:43:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity buckets & deal rhythm — weekly orchestration

Thanks Jordan — quick infra notes below before we populate: 

1) Lead times: for Dedicated reservation pools we need 3 full business weeks to reserve GPU capacity and run provisioning validation (OS/images, KMS, network ACLs). For private deployments (on-prem/VPC) add 2 additional weeks for customer network approvals.

2) Quantization/Model tradeoffs: if a deal is flexible on model variant (e.g., FP16 -> Q4/Q5 quantized), we can reduce slot counts by ~30% in bucket sizing. Call that out in the template.

3) Burst capacity: Current burst pool has 40% spare headroom for December; if more than two top-6 deals stretch into December we will need to reprioritize committed reservations.

Action for me: I'll annotate the template with provisioning lead time flags and a short infra-risk column ("provision_risk: low/med/high").

Michael
Director, Infrastructure & Ops
Redwood Inference

Thanks Sophie — and good to have procurement looped in. Short plan and next steps so this thread can be acted on immediately: 

Summary of constraints:
- Dedicated pool reservation lead time: 3 business weeks. Cutoff for December provisioning: 2026-11-24 (we need the committed reservation request in HubSpot + signed SOW by then).
- Private deployment adds ~2 weeks for network approvals; cutoff for December private: 2026-11-17.
- Quantized variants OK; note potential SLA delta in latency (we will include a 95thpct latency estimate in the consolidated sheet).

Concrete next steps (owner — due):
- Ben Carter — populate the capacity_buckets_template.xlsx with burst eligibility, token share, and suggested bucket (due 2026-11-08 18:00 PT).
- Laura Bennett — confirm finance burn threshold and mark any deals that need exec credit approval (due 2026-11-09 noon PT).
- Jordan Blake — confirm with Acme whether a quantized model is acceptable and capture SLA acceptance (due 2026-11-09 EOD PT).
- Michael Grant — I will add provisioning_risk and the cutoff calendar entries to the sheet, then push the consolidated doc to Sophie on 2026-11-09 morning.

If anyone expects blockers meeting these dates, flag now so we can propose a fallback (deferred GA launch / partial burst + fallback to hosted).

Mike

Redwood Inference
